about.title: How this site is built
about.lead: A static React app that teaches Ergo with live mainnet data — no backend, no database, no tracking.
about.intro: Learn Me An Ergo is a single-page app. Everything runs in your browser: the pages are plain files, and the live numbers — blocks, transactions, addresses, charts — are fetched straight from a public Ergo explorer API. There is no server of our own and nothing to log in to.

stack.title: The stack
stack.react: Renders every page, article and interactive demo.
stack.vite: Dev server with instant reload, and the production build.
stack.tailwind: All styling, as utility classes plus a small stylesheet for article typography.
stack.i18next: English and Vietnamese: UI strings and every article's text live in JSON files.
stack.noble: blake2b256 in the browser, used to rebuild address checksums and ids.
stack.oxlint: Fast linting for the whole codebase.

data.title: Where the data comes from
data.api: Live data comes from the REST API of explorer.erg.vn (Ergo Vietnam), called directly from your browser. Network stats refresh on a timer; nothing is cached or proxied by this site. The NiPoPoW article also asks two public Ergo nodes (sv1.erg.vn, sv2.erg.vn) for a live proof.
data.protocol: Protocol logic — Base58, address encoding, the emission schedule, EIP-27 — is re-implemented in plain JavaScript and checked against real blocks, so the tools can show every step instead of calling a black box.

i18n.title: Two languages
i18n.p1: The site is fully bilingual. Interface strings live in src/locales/en.json and vi.json. Each article is a single React component whose text sits in its own JSON pair and loads lazily with the article, so a page only downloads the language it needs. A small script checks that both languages have the same keys, tags and variables.

design.title: Design for reading
design.p1: Article typography and the light/dark palettes are adapted from the <paper>hugo-paper</paper> theme (MIT): a warm paper background, 18px text with generous line height and a narrow reading column. Every text colour is checked against WCAG AA contrast in both themes. Fonts (Be Vietnam Pro and JetBrains Mono) are self-hosted, so no request goes to a font CDN.

build.title: Build and hosting
build.p1: npm run build first generates sitemap.xml, robots.txt and llms.txt from the article and tool lists, then Vite bundles the app. Articles and tools are split into separate chunks and loaded on demand.
build.p2: The output is a folder of static files. Any static host works; the only rule needed is a fallback that serves index.html for every path, included for both Vercel and Netlify-style hosts. Social preview images are rendered once with headless Chrome and committed.

source.title: Open source
source.p1: The full source is on <repo>GitHub</repo>. Corrections to the articles are especially welcome — please update both languages. See the <privacy>privacy page</privacy> for exactly what the site does and doesn't do with your data.

addressDecoder.checksumDoesNotMatchTheAddress: Checksum does NOT match — the address is mistyped or corrupted.
addressDecoder.checksumMatchesTheAddressIsValid: Checksum matches — the address is valid.
addressDecoder.ergoAddressesUseTheBase58Alphabet: Ergo addresses use the Base58 alphabet (no 0, O, I or l).
addressDecoder.forP2sTheAddressContentIs: For P2S, the address content is the entire ErgoTree.
addressDecoder.n0x00MainnetP2pkAddressesStartWith: 0x00 = mainnet (P2PK addresses start with “9”), 0x10 = testnet (they start with “3”).
addressDecoder.p2shOnlyHoldsAHashOf: P2SH only holds a hash of the script, so the ErgoTree can’t be recovered from the address — the spender must reveal the script when spending.
addressDecoder.prefixNetworkTypeAddressTypeThe: prefix = network type + address type. The high nibble is the network, the low nibble is the type.
addressDecoder.theStringIsReallyOneBig: The string is really one big number written in base 58. Converting it to hex gives {{length}} bytes:
addressDecoder.viewThisAddressInTheExplorer: View this address in the explorer
addressDecoder.withBlake2b256AndTakeTheFirst: with blake2b256 and take the first 4 bytes. Mistype even a single character and the checksum won’t match.

addressPage.balanceExplained: A “balance” isn’t stored anywhere — it is the total value of the {{boxes}} unspent boxes locked by this address.
addressPage.theScriptThatActuallyLocksThe: The script that actually locks the boxes. An address is just a human-friendly encoding of the ErgoTree.
addressPage.thisAddressHasNeverAppearedOn: This address has never appeared on the blockchain.
addressPage.thisAddressHasNoUnspentBoxes: This address has no unspent boxes left — its balance is 0.

blake2b.always32Bytes64HexCharacters: Always 32 bytes (64 hex characters), no matter how long the input is. Try changing “Ergo” to “ergo”: the result changes completely.
blake2b.theFirst4BytesOfBlake2b256: the first 4 bytes of blake2b256(prefix ‖ content); P2SH uses the first 24 bytes of the script hash.
blake2b.useOnlyTheCharacters09: Use only the characters 0–9 and a–f, with an even number of characters (each byte = 2 characters).
blake2b.usesBlake2b256AsTheHashFunction: uses blake2b256 as the hash function inside the mining algorithm.

blockPage.autolykosV1AOneTimePublic: Autolykos v1: a one-time public key the miner generated for this block.
blockPage.autolykosV1TheKSumSolution: Autolykos v1: the k-sum solution value d; it must be below the target b.
blockPage.blake2b256OfTheSerializedHeaderChange: blake2b256 of the serialized header. Change any single byte and the id changes completely.
blockPage.eip27ThisPartIsLocked: EIP-27: this part is locked into the re-emission contract and paid out to miners after the main emission ends.
blockPage.equivalentToThSOfNetwork: Equivalent to ~{{v0}} TH/s of network hashrate at 2-minute blocks.
blockPage.merkleRootOfTheBlockS: Merkle root of the block's transactions.
blockPage.merkleRootOfTheExtensionSection: Merkle root of the extension section: network parameters, NiPoPoW interlinks.
blockPage.n3BytesMinersUseToVote: 3 bytes miners use to vote on parameter changes (0 = no vote).
blockPage.newErgCreatedAtThisHeight: New ERG created at this height according to the emission schedule.
blockPage.rootOfTheStateChangeProofs: Root of the state-change proofs (authenticated dictionary proofs).
blockPage.the33ByteDigestOfThe: The 33-byte digest of the AVL+ tree holding the entire UTXO set after this block — it lets “light” nodes verify state.
blockPage.the8BytesAMinerKeeps: The 8 bytes a miner keeps changing until the hash meets the target.
blockPage.theHeaderSProtocolVersionIt: The header's protocol version; it goes up with each network upgrade (e.g. v2 activated Autolykos v2).
blockPage.theIdOfThePreviousBlock: The id of the previous block — the link that chains blocks into a blockchain.
blockPage.theMinerSPublicKeyThe: The miner's public key — the reward is locked to this key.
blockPage.theTargetDifficultyInCompactForm: The target difficulty in compact form.
blockPage.unusedInAutolykosV2ItHolds: Unused in Autolykos v2; it holds the secp256k1 generator point G.
blockPage.whenTheMinerCreatedTheBlock: When the miner created the block, in Unix milliseconds.

boxPage.aFreeRegisterForEip4: A free register. For EIP-4 tokens, R5 usually holds the description.
boxPage.aFreeRegisterForEip42: A free register. For EIP-4 tokens, R6 usually holds the number of decimals.
boxPage.aFreeRegisterR4R9Contracts: A free register (R4–R9) — contracts define their own meaning.
boxPage.boxExplained: A box is Ergo’s unit of state: a “box” holding ERG, tokens and data, locked by a script. It can only be spent once, in full.
boxPage.boxIdBlake2b256OfTheBox: Box id = blake2b256 of the box's full contents, and (txId, index) makes every box unique.
boxPage.notYetTheBoxIsStill: not yet — the box is still a UTXO
boxPage.theAmountOfErgInThe: The amount of ERG in the box, stored in nanoERG ({{v0}}).
boxPage.theErgotreeLockingTheBoxIt: The ErgoTree locking the box. It corresponds to the address
boxPage.theFirstFreeRegisterForEip: The first free register. For EIP-4 tokens, R4 usually holds the token name.
boxPage.thisBoxUsesNoCustomRegisters: This box uses no custom registers.

emissionCalculator.dropsBy3ErgEvery64: Drops by 3 ERG every 64,800 blocks (~3 months); part of it is locked into the re-emission contract.
emissionCalculator.extrapolatedFromTheLatestBlockAt: Extrapolated from the latest block at 2 minutes per block.
emissionCalculator.fromBlockThisPartGoesInto: From block {{v0}}, this part goes into the re-emission contract instead of straight to the miner: 12 ERG if the reward is ≥ 15 ERG, otherwise (reward − 3).
emissionCalculator.mainEmissionIsOverMinersReceive: Main emission is over; miners receive 3 ERG/block from the re-emission contract (EIP-27).
emissionCalculator.n3ErgPerBlockPaidFrom: 3 ERG per block paid from the re-emission contract until it runs dry.
emissionCalculator.n75ErgPerBlockForThe: 75 ERG per block for the first ~2 years (525,600 blocks).
emissionCalculator.summedFromBlock1ToBlock: Summed from block 1 to block {{v0}}. The supply can never exceed {{v1}} ERG.
emissionCalculator.theAmountOfNewErgCreated: The amount of new ERG created by the emission contract at this block.
emissionCalculator.theRewardDropsBy3Erg: The reward drops by 3 ERG every 64,800 blocks (~3 months).
emissionCalculator.theShareForTheDevelopmentTreasury: The share for the development treasury during roughly the first 2.5 years (7.5 ERG/block, then 4.5 and 1.5 ERG).
emissionCalculator.thisBlockHasAlreadyBeenMined: This block has already been mined — the actual date may differ by a few days because block times vary.

privacy.articlesLinkToOutsideMaterialDocs: Articles link to outside material (docs.ergoplatform.com, GitHub, blogs, papers). Once you click through, that site’s privacy policy applies.
privacy.blocksTransactionsAddressesTokensChartsU: Blocks, transactions, addresses, tokens, charts — used on most pages. The explorer states a no-logging policy.
privacy.fontsAreServedFromThisDomain: Fonts are served from this domain, not loaded from Google Fonts or any other CDN.
privacy.openYourBrowserSDeveloperTools: Open your browser’s developer tools (F12), the Network tab, and reload: you will only see requests to this domain and to *.erg.vn.
privacy.pageCallsThemToFetchA: page calls them, to fetch a real proof.
privacy.theSiteIsASetOf: The site is a set of static files. The hosting provider may keep standard technical logs (IP address, time, path) for a short period for operations and abuse protection; we do not use, export or combine those logs with anything to identify readers.
privacy.theSiteWritesJustTwoPreferences: The site writes just two preferences to your browser’s local storage: your language (EN/VI) and light/dark theme. Those values stay on your device, are never sent anywhere, and disappear when you clear site data.
privacy.thisSiteIsAFreeLearning: This site is a free learning resource. It doesn’t need to know who you are, and it is built so that it can’t.
privacy.toShowRealNumbersYourBrowser: To show real numbers, your browser calls two Ergo data services run by Ergo Vietnam directly. Like any web request, those servers see your IP address and the API path requested (for example “latest blocks”), but they receive nothing about you from this site.

pubkeyToAddress.aCompressedPublicKeyMustBe: A compressed public key must be exactly 33 bytes (66 hex characters); you entered {{length}} bytes
pubkeyToAddress.encodeWithBase58ToGetA: Encode with Base58 to get a readable string without easily confused characters like 0/O and I/l.
pubkeyToAddress.takeTheFirst4BytesOf: Take the first 4 bytes of the hash as the checksum.
pubkeyToAddress.theContentOfAP2pkAddress: The content of a P2PK address is simply the 33-byte public key.
pubkeyToAddress.theFirstByteOfACompressed: The first byte of a compressed key must be 02 or 03 (it tells whether the y coordinate is even or odd)
pubkeyToAddress.theScriptThatActuallyLocksBoxes: The script that actually locks boxes sent to this address: “prove you know the secret key behind this public key”.

tokenPage.equalToTheIdOfThe: Equal to the id of the first input box of the issuing transaction — so no two tokens can share an id.
tokenPage.theBlockchainStoresOnlyIntegersThe: The blockchain stores only integers; the {{decimals}} decimal places (R6) are a display convention.
tokenPage.theFirstBoxHoldingTheToken: The first box holding the token; its R4–R6 hold the name, description and decimals.

tools.everyCalculationRunsRightInYour: Every calculation runs right in your browser — nothing is sent to a server.

txPage.blockRewardTransactionNewErgComes: Block reward transaction: new ERG comes from the emission contract.
txPage.ergoHasNoBitcoinStyleCoinbase: Ergo has no Bitcoin-style coinbase: the reward transaction spends the emission contract’s box and recreates it with less ERG, so ERG is still conserved.
txPage.idExplained: blake2b256 of the serialized transaction without its signatures (proofs) — so signatures can never change the id.
txPage.inputsAreBoxesBeingDestroyedOutputs: Inputs are boxes being destroyed; outputs are newly created boxes. Data inputs are only read, never spent.
txPage.inputsOutputsNoErgWasCreated: Inputs = Outputs: no ERG was created or destroyed.
txPage.n0001ErgIsTypicalThe: 0.001 ERG is typical (the node’s default minimum). The wallet sets the fee, and miners prioritize transactions by fee per byte.
txPage.theDifferenceComesFromBoxesThat: The difference comes from boxes that are not indexed yet.
txPage.unlikeBitcoinAnErgoFeeIs: Unlike Bitcoin, an Ergo fee is not the “leftover” — it is a separate output locked by the fee contract. The block’s miner collects the fee boxes into a reward box, which stays locked for 720 blocks.

units.ergHasAtMost9Decimal: ERG has at most 9 decimal places (1 nanoERG = 0.000000001 ERG)

units.numbersOnlyWithADotFor: Numbers only, with a dot for the decimal part
units.theBlockchainDoesnTStoreDecimals: The blockchain doesn’t store decimals. Every box’s value is a 64-bit integer measured in
